product: NdPr oxide, refined into NdFeB permanent magnets, plus separated heavies (Dy, Tb, Gd, Sm). Demand comes from EV traction motors (GM), consumer electronics and recycling (Apple), robots, drones (Project Swarm), data centers and aerospace/defense (2026-08-06).
demand: Volume-led. Q2 2026 NdPr sales rose 127% y/y to 1,006 MT and production 41% to 840 MT; Materials segment revenue +155% y/y. Price contributes modestly: Q3 realized NdPr pricing guided high-$90s/kg plus roughly $10/kg PPA income (2026-08-06).
pricing_power: A fall in NdPr price or loss of the DoD floor and PPA income; Independence and 10X startup overhead not yet inventoriable; fixed-cost under-absorption if throughput stalls; chemical cost inflation, with sulfuric acid doubled (2026-08-06, 2026-09-09).
competition: China low-cost NdPr and finished magnets are the substitute but are export-controlled, with heavy-rare-earth flows near zero into the US and Japan. Rare-earth-free and ferrite designs substitute for some uses, but management argues robotics torque-density needs make substitution hard (2026-08-06).

web_bottleneck: NdPr oxide supply outside China. Management calls NdPr the binding constraint; only MP and Lynas are scaled ex-China producers, and announced Western magnet capacity would need NdPr output to roughly double (2026-08-06, 2026-09-09). Heavy-rare-earth separation, metallization and skilled labor are secondary constraints (2026-08-06).
web_who_benefits_next: GM and Apple (foundational magnet customers), US drone makers via Project Swarm, the Department of War and defense primes, robotics and physical-AI builders, Lynas as the only other scaled ex-China NdPr producer, and downstream US motor and magnet makers plus the Japan supply chain (2026-08-06).
web_who_loses: China rare-earth and magnet export complex, which loses leverage and volume as the West onshores; Chinese magnet and heavy-rare-earth exporters; Western magnet startups that lack their own NdPr feedstock (2026-08-06).
web_margin_collapse_risk: A fall in NdPr price or loss of the DoD floor and PPA income; Independence and 10X startup overhead not yet inventoriable; fixed-cost under-absorption if throughput stalls; chemical cost inflation, with sulfuric acid doubled (2026-08-06, 2026-09-09).

web_ceo_promised: 2026-08-06 CEO James Litinsky: begin commercial magnet shipments to GM in the fourth quarter of 2026, and produce Dy/Tb product later this year. 2026-09-09 CFO Ryan Corbett: bring 10X into production at the end of 2028 (earnings call and Jefferies conference).
web_did_they_deliver: Q2 2026 delivered: NdPr production 840 MT (+41%) and sales 1,006 MT (+127%), called consistent with expectations despite an extended April shutdown; the DoD price floor generated $17.6M PPA income; the nine-figure gadolinium offtake was signed July 2026 (2026-08-06).
web_what_would_falsify: Failure to begin commercial GM magnet shipments in Q4 2026, or Dy/Tb slipping past 2026; NdPr volume growth stalling well below the 127% y/y pace; a successful legal or legislative challenge to the DoD equity/floor-price authority; realized NdPr price falling below the floor with no offsetting PPA.
